texts: good. fireable rule carrying the Keeper, the harvesting, the new moon and 'that salt-bloom', with 'stays potent' recorded as a continuing state plus a plain 'is potent' fact.
good. the 'gathers' wording parses as cleanly as the 'harvests' one — condition, bound 'that salt-bloom', and the continuing potency are all present in a fireable rule.

good. 'every time' gives a per-occasion rule and the change of kind is fully carried: the bloom turns, the chalky residue is recorded as its resulting state, and both 'chalky' and 'residue' are linked. (Worth knowing: 'at the full moon' is stored as a plain named time, so it will not order or compare against calendar dates.)

mixed: all the content is there and the rule fires, but the turning is keyed to the salt-bloom rather than to each gathering, so two gatherings of the same bloom would collapse into a single turning instead of one per occasion. Your wording is not the cause — the identical sentence with 'full moon' was keyed correctly — so keep it as written.
